entry 2026-11-20 21:35, 'for the planner': 'HasChronalNeighbour ↔ ChronalNeighbours bridge lemma'

Causal/LadderLocal.lean SCOPE: 'ChronalNeighbours asks chronology inside each open V, not in M. [...] under absolute minimality on a T1 space it is exactly I^±(x) ≠ ∅ for every x (AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalPastNeighbours_iff). It is not HasChronalNeighbour of the Causal.LocateExtension (one point, one side, chronology in M).'

hypotheses.paper: ChronalNeighbours (every v of every open V has p, p' ∈ V with p ≪_V v ≪_V p')
hypotheses.note: the conclusion HasChronalNeighbour p at every p is drawn from the future half alone (V = M); the past half gives it too, and both halves give the two-sided NonemptyChronalCones. Stronger than asked: a chronological past in every open V ∋ p (ChronalPastNeighbours.Iminus_nonempty_of_mem), which HasChronalNeighbour (chronology in M) cannot express.

findings: ChronalNeighbours ⇒ NonemptyChronalCones ⇒ HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere, each strict (the closed half-line for the second, globalLine for the first, see 1-minimal and 3-converse): three strengths of chronology, of which LadderLocal.lean:93-94 names the two ends.
questions: The target's 'HasChronalNeighbour everywhere' is read as '∀ p : M, C.HasChronalNeighbour p' (chronology in M, one side), named HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere for the ladder; whether it (or the two-sided NonemptyChronalCones) becomes a ladder node is OQ-51's question, not settled here.

source.statement: target T-abs-chronal-neighbour-bridge, title and evidence (the form to be formalized)

Causal/LadderLocal.lean SCOPE: 'ChronalNeighbours asks chronology inside each open V, not in M. [...] under absolute minimality on a T1 space it is exactly I^±(x) ≠ ∅ for every x (AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalPastNeighbours_iff). It is not HasChronalNeighbour of the Causal.LocateExtension (one point, one side, chronology in M).'
comment on [[property]] chronal_neighbours: 'under absolute minimality on a T1 space it is I^±(x) ≠ ∅ for every x (… chronalPastNeighbours_iff, past side)'

hypotheses.note: necessary: globalLine (on ℝ, Hausdorff and second countable; x ≪_U y iff U = ℝ and x < y) is T1 with non-empty chronological cones and push-up, causally open and causal, but without chronal past neighbours (0 has no past in (−1, ∞)), hence not absolutely minimal (globalLine_separates; bare form not_chronalNeighbours_of_t1_bare).

necessary: on the Sierpiński space Prop (only {True} open besides ∅ and univ) every cover contains ⊤, so every causality is absolutely minimal; sierpinskiCausality (x ≪_U y iff U = ⊤) has non-empty cones and no chronal past neighbours ({True} has no chronology) (sierpinskiCausality_separates, which also derives ¬ T1Space Prop; bare forms not_chronalNeighbours_of_absolutelyMinimal_bare and, for the strict LadderLocal lemma, not_chronalPastNeighbours_of_absolutelyMinimal_bare). Not one of ETT's spacetimes (not T1).

CausallyArcConnected.chronalNeighbours_iff: the same equivalence under causal arc-connectedness alone, with no separation axiom (an initial piece of a chronal curve from q ≪ v lies in any open V ∋ v: CausallyArcConnectedOn.Iminus_nonempty_of_le). Arc-connectedness implies absolute minimality, so this is the T1-free special case.

findings: The T1 hypothesis of the strict Causal.Causality.AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalPastNeighbours_iff (Causal/LadderLocal.lean:319) cannot be dropped (not_chronalPastNeighbours_of_absolutelyMinimal_bare, the Sierpiński space), nor absolute minimality (globalLine_not_chronalPastNeighbours with globalLine_nonemptyChronalCones on the T1 space ℝ): its SCOPE sentence (LadderLocal.lean:90-93) is sharp.

Under causal arc-connectedness the characterisation needs no separation axiom (CausallyArcConnected.chronalNeighbours_iff), which the ladder comment at programme/ladder.toml:236-240 does not record: an edge causally_arc_connected ∧ nonempty_chronal_cones ⇒ chronal_neighbours with no standing.

globalLine (≪ in ℝ only) is causal, causally open and has push-up and non-empty chronological cones, and is not absolutely minimal: in a /tmp simulation of programme/ladder.toml it settles 10 pairs now unknown (causally_open, causally_open_future, locally_causally_open, locally_causally_open_future ⇏ absolutely_minimal and ⇏ causally_arc_connected; push_up, locally_push_up ⇏ absolutely_minimal).
questions: 'I⁺(x) and I⁻(x) non-empty' is read in M, as C.Iplus ⊤ {x} and C.Iminus ⊤ {x}, as in Zplus_Zminus_eq_univ and K_lorentzien; chronology in the open sets is what ChronalNeighbours adds.

hypotheses.paper: exists_leaving: M preconnected, C causally arc-connected, O open, non-empty, O ≠ univ

Also with HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (exists_leaving_of_hasChronalNeighbourEverywhere), the weakest of the named forms.

hypotheses.paper: exists_leaving_of_isOpenEmbedding: ι open embedding, N non-empty, range ι ≠ univ, M preconnected, causally arc-connected
hypotheses.note: conclusion verbatim (D = C or C.dual, the curve chronal in range ι on every [0, s], s < 1)

hypotheses.paper: (beyond the target) causal arc-connectedness of M
hypotheses.note: exists_leaving_of_locallyCausallyArcConnected(_of_chronalPastNeighbours): local causal arc-connectedness and chronal (past) neighbours suffice, since the chronology is in every open set; no absolute minimality. With absolute minimality, local arc-connectedness is arc-connectedness (LocallyCausallyArcConnected.causallyArcConnected), so the gain is on non-absolutely-minimal spacetimes only; no example of one with chronal neighbours is given, and strictness is not claimed.

questions: 'exists_leaving restated with ChronalNeighbours' is read as: the boundary hypothesis ∀ p ∈ frontier O, HasChronalNeighbour p replaced by C.ChronalNeighbours, every other hypothesis and the conclusion kept; exists_leaving_of_isOpenEmbedding, futureBoundary_union_pastBoundary_nonempty and frontier_subset_closure_boundary likewise.

hypotheses.paper: (the converse) HasChronalNeighbour at every point ⇒ ChronalNeighbours
hypotheses.note: refuted even with T1, M preconnected and causal arc-connectedness (hence absolute minimality): the closed half-line [0, ∞) (Causal.closedHalfLine, LocateExtension.lean:758), every point of which has a chronological future while I⁻(0) = ∅; so it is not NonemptyChronalCones either, and in AbsolutelyMinimal.chronalNeighbours_iff the two-sided cones cannot be one-sided. Bare form for X : Type.

findings: The converse of ChronalNeighbours ⇒ HasChronalNeighbour-everywhere fails on a T1 (indeed Hausdorff, second countable), preconnected, causally arc-connected spacetime (closedHalfLine_separates_chronalNeighbours); the failure is one-sidedness at a single point, as at a BTZ point.

definitions.what: every point has a chronal neighbour in M, to the future or to the past (∀ p, HasChronalNeighbour p)

every point has a non-empty chronological future and past in M (∀ x, I⁺(x) ≠ ∅ ∧ I⁻(x) ≠ ∅); up to the bound name the inline hI of Causal.Causality.Zplus_Zminus_eq_univ, K_lorentzien, K_eq_I_of_pushUp

fails.note: the closed half-line (Hausdorff, second countable, preconnected; T1 and absolutely minimal stated); through the closure also ⇏ chronal_neighbours, and absolutely_minimal ∧ has_chronal_neighbour ⇏ either
the same witness, its last conjunct; through the closure also ⇏ causally_arc_connected

the Sierpiński space Prop, not T1 (stated: ¬ T1Space Prop); the Mathlib instances found on Prop are CompactSpace and SecondCountableTopology (T0Space and ConnectedSpace are not synthesised). Read only against edges without T1 standing: it shows the T1 of the edge above is needed
also ¬ ChronalNeighbours conjoined: settles causally_plain → chronal_neighbours (unknown today)

the same with a chronal neighbour at every point
∂⁺O ∪ ∂⁻O is dense in ∂O for every open O

for_keeper.simulation: On /tmp/cnb_sim/ladder.toml (a copy of programme/ladder.toml at 2026-11-21 with the two properties, the four [[implies]] and the six [[fails]] above appended), `python3 tools/ladder.py check --file` reports 12 violations, all 'not found in lean-causal' (scaffold names, until graduation), and no contradiction; `matrix --file` turns 11 ordered pairs of today's properties from unknown to fails (causally_plain ⇏ chronal_neighbours; causally_open, causally_open_future, locally_causally_open, locally_causally_open_future ⇏ absolutely_minimal and ⇏ causally_arc_connected; push_up, locally_push_up ⇏ absolutely_minimal) and classifies 48 of the 74 well-typed new pairs (45 fails, 3 implied; 26 unknown, all from has_chronal_neighbour or nonempty_chronal_cones to a node other than chronal_neighbours, absolutely_minimal, causally_arc_connected, globally_hyperbolic, causally_compact).

kb_proposals: A causality whose chronology lives only in M (Causal.globalLine: x ≪_U y iff U = ℝ and x < y) is causal, causally open, push-up, with non-empty chronological cones, and not absolutely minimal: the cheap separation of anything read off ≪ in M from absolute minimality and from chronology in every open set (CausalScaffold.ChronalNeighbourBridge, T-abs-chronal-neighbour-bridge).

On the Sierpiński space Prop every open containing False is ⊤ (nhds_false), so every cover contains ⊤ and every causality is absolutely minimal: a cheap non-T1 witness that a T1 hypothesis is used (Causal.sierpinskiCausality; Mathlib synthesises CompactSpace and SecondCountableTopology on Prop, not T0Space).

Chronology at points has three strengths: HasChronalNeighbourEverywhere (one side, in M) < NonemptyChronalCones (both sides, in M) < ChronalNeighbours (both sides, in every open); the last two agree under causal arc-connectedness with no separation, or under absolute minimality on a T1 space, and neither hypothesis can be dropped (CausalScaffold.ChronalNeighbourBridge).
